items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 19 at 4:47AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:

items.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 19 at 4:22AM AKDT until September 20 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Chena River Basin from Moose Creek Dam to the end of Chena
Hot Springs Road.

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable. River and stream flows
remain elevated. Ponding of water in areas is occurring or is
imminent.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued September 19 at 4:04AM AKDT until September 20 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:

items.headline: High Wind Watch issued September 19 at 4:04AM AKDT until September 21 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph
possible.

* WHERE...Haines Borough and Klukwan and Municipality of Skagway.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...High winds could blow around unsecured objects, damage
property and cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will quickly increase as a strong low
pressure system moves into the northern gulf. Confidence has
increased on strong wind gusts around 50 to 60 mph
items.areas: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan
items.instruction:
People are urged to secure vessels and loose objects that could be
blown around or damaged by the wind.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

items.headline: Flood Watch issued September 19 at 2:52AM AKDT until September 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
A series of low pressures will move through the panhandle this
weekend bringing prolonged rain combined with high freezing levels to
increase ice melt on glacier river systems. The heavy rainfall and
associated runoff will produce significant river rises with the
potential of minor flooding.

possible.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 18 at 4:14PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

High water in the Kuskokwim River region will continue over the next
few days. Conditions are expected to become favorable for water
levels to gradually recede over the weekend and into the middle of
next week.

including, but not limited to: Kwethluk, Bethel, Oscarville,
Napaskiak, Napkiak, Kasigluk, Nunapitchuk, and Atmauluak.
